title: Unix and C portability from local operating system to cross-machine software substrate
pressure: Time-sharing and minicomputers needed usable operating environments, while machine-specific assembly made systems difficult to move and maintain.
preExistingWorldModel: Multics demonstrated rich time-sharing at high complexity/cost; Bell Labs had minicomputers and systems researchers.
candidateRoutes: rewrite Unix in a systems language
observationsAndInstruments: C combined systems-level control with greater portability and Unix was rewritten in C.
AT&T licensing and university/BSD distribution carried Unix across hardware families.
Networking and tooling accumulated around Unix rather than being one original monolith.
decisiveTests: preserve useful performance/control after a machine port
allow local source adaptation rather than binary cloning
separate portable interfaces from device-specific code
technicalOrScientificTransition: Executable systems knowledge became portable across machines and institutions through C, source distribution and a modular operating environment.
rivalsAndFailures: Portability never meant zero machine-specific code.
Unix fragmentation later created standards pressure.
A smaller system could outrun a more ambitious predecessor without being globally feature-complete.
diffusionAndScaling: Diffusion depended on complements, cost/yield/standards and institutional adoption; the nominal breakthrough date did not equal broad effective use.
standardsAndInstitutions: Laboratories, firms, standard bodies, regulators, users and infrastructure operators owned different parts of evidence, implementation and consequence.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Lifecycle harms and authority changes are preserved where evidenced rather than inferred from local technical success.
secondOrderEffects: Executable systems knowledge became portable across machines and institutions through C, source distribution and a modular operating environment.
sourceNativeSummary: Executable systems knowledge became portable across machines and institutions through C, source distribution and a modular operating environment.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement most constrained diffusion at each lifecycle phase?
Which later narrative compresses materially distributed work?
